entries.clue: A comically dim notion's getting repeated censure (11)

annotation.definitionFit: A sweet child is an angelic one: charming and good-natured.

entries.clue: Group stitching up conductors (8)

blocks.note: a sort is a kind or group
a seam is a line of stitching

annotation.surface: A sewing circle is at work on something.
annotation.walkthrough: "Stitching up" reads as one phrase meaning to sew or to frame someone; here "up" works alone, turning SORT + SEAM upside down.

entries.clue: Loudly appreciates quality of wine (4)

indicators.note: something said loudly is spoken out, so we go by its sound

blocks.note: to appreciate a fact is to understand it; say that synonym aloud

annotation.surface: A wine lover is noisily praising a fine vintage.
annotation.walkthrough: "Loudly appreciates" pictures a gushing wine taster; "appreciates" really means understands, which is KNOWS.
annotation.definitionFit: A wine's nose is its aroma, one of the qualities tasters judge.

entries.clue: After time, hack desires to assemble children's novel (3,7)

annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the answer is one particular children's book, Roald Dahl's 1983 novel about child-hating witches.

entries.clue: Not neat – put off (2,3)

blocks.note: a neat spirit comes with nothing added; this is the opposite, a drink chilled with cubes

annotation.surface: Someone is repelled by untidiness.
annotation.walkthrough: "Not neat" suggests untidiness, but it is bar talk: a neat spirit is served with nothing added.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one idiom: a drink with ice added is not neat, and a plan frozen for later has been put off.

entries.clue: Oaf does off with sprats, etc. (7)

annotation.surface: A clumsy fellow wanders off carrying little fish.
annotation.walkthrough: Sprats are small herring-like fish; "etc." makes them one example of a whole class, which is why the definition is fair.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: sprats are small edible sea fish, and "etc." widens them to the whole category.

entries.clue: Public events: a detergent's sprayed after Everyman's seen (4-3-6)

the anagram goes after ME, so ME comes first

anagram fodder; the 's gives the S

annotation.walkthrough: A setter naming himself in the clue means ME (or I). The rest is an anagram of eleven letters.

entries.clue: Magenta and Ted vow to order basic meal (4,3,3,3)

anagram fodder; "and" just joins the two parts

annotation.walkthrough: "And" is not in the fodder: MAGENTA + TED VOW is thirteen letters, the length of the answer. Meat and two veg is a British phrase for a plain traditional dinner.
annotation.definitionFit: Meat and two veg is the stock plain British dinner, so a basic meal.

entries.clue: Who might issue tweets about primarily 'tremendous' golf scores? (7)

indicators.note: take the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: an eagle is two under par on a golf hole
first letter of tremendous

annotation.surface: A sports star posts social-media tweets bragging about tremendous golf scores.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is social media, but tweets are also birdsong: young birds chirp. The question mark signals the definition is by example.
annotation.definitionFit: Eaglets are young eagles, and a chick's cheeping can be called tweeting.

entries.clue: Greek character with old poem about Arabian land (7)

RIME is an old spelling of rhyme, as in The Rime of the Ancient Mariner

annotation.surface: A figure from Greek legend features in an ancient poem about Arabia.
annotation.walkthrough: "About" looks like it means concerning, the poem's subject; it is the reversal signal, applied to the whole string. The old spelling survives in Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner.
annotation.definitionFit: An emirate is a state ruled by an emir, such as those of the Arabian peninsula.

entries.clue: Small drink the French consumed with vacant expression? (2,3)

annotation.definitionFit: "To let" is what a sign says on a vacant house or flat available to rent.

entries.clue: Spooner's to accumulate bulk: it's a reckoning point (8)

annotation.walkthrough: "To accumulate bulk" reads as one idea, gaining weight; it is two words, each trading its first sound with the other's.

entries.clue: Reindeer herders all ran and sped in a frenzy (10)

anagram fodder; "and" only joins

annotation.walkthrough: "And" stays out of the fodder: ALL RAN + SPED is exactly ten letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Laplanders, the Sami of northern Scandinavia, are traditionally reindeer herders.

entries.clue: Novel may concern sorcery (10)

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: A book might be about magic.
annotation.walkthrough: "Novel" is the anagram signal, not a book, though the surface reads it as one.
annotation.definitionFit: Necromancy, strictly calling up the dead, is used for black magic or sorcery generally.

entries.clue: Foremost of old deities in Norse? (4)

indicators.note: take the foremost, that is first, letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: first letters of old, deities, in, Norse

annotation.surface: A question about who led the ancient gods of Norse myth.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: Odin was chief of the Norse gods. The question mark flags the double duty.
annotation.definitionFit: Odin was the chief of the old Norse gods, the foremost deity.

entries.clue: Pretty much perfectly – or OK? (4,4)

blocks.note: done almost flawlessly, to a high standard
a formal way of agreeing, as in "all right, I'll do it"

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether a job was nearly flawless or merely all right.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sets the two senses against each other as a grading question; the same phrase answers both.
annotation.definitionFit: "Very well" means excellently, and as a reply it means OK, I agree.

entries.clue: Yawn, partly concealing a peeve (4)

annotation.walkthrough: "Concealing" is part of the hiding place, not the indicator; the letters run across it and the next two words.
annotation.definitionFit: To gape is to open the mouth wide, as in a yawn.

entries.clue: Exercise before feast including seconds (5-2)

indicators.note: including means taking something in, so the S goes inside PRE + SUP

blocks.note: pre- means before
S is the abbreviation for seconds
to sup is to eat or dine

annotation.surface: Some exercise before a big meal, including second helpings.
annotation.walkthrough: "Before" looks like it joins the exercise to the feast in time; it is PRE. "Seconds" suggests extra helpings, but it is S. A press-up is the British name for a push-up.
annotation.definitionFit: A British regional term: this is what Americans call a push-up, a floor exercise raising the body with the arms.

entries.clue: Decent odds on getting good choral service (8)

entries.clue: Take a spoon to porridge (4)

annotation.definitionFit: To stir is to take a spoon to something, and stir, like porridge, means prison time.
